units.text: INT. CIRCUIT COURT HALLWAY - AFTERNOON
A long terrazzo corridor lined with scarred oak benches, each with a brass nameplate for a donor nobody remembers.
Fluorescent tubes hum overhead.
A radiator under a tall window knocks twice and goes silent.
Through the glass, a parking structure and a gray sky.
On the bench nearest the courtroom doors, ROSALIND HARTE, 58, sits upright in a navy suit that fit better ten years ago.
Her hands hold a plastic folder closed on her lap.
Her reading glasses hang from a chain, untouched.
Next to her but not touching, her son ELIAS HARTE, 31, hunches forward, elbows on his knees, a county-issue lanyard around his neck, his hair cut short by someone else.
He picks at a thread on his cuff.
At the water fountain, leaning with arms crossed, is ATTORNEY NOEL BASHIR, 40s, in a charcoal suit and a tie loosened half an inch.
He has been standing there for some time.
You haven't eaten.
units.name: ROSALIND

units.text: I'm fine.
units.name: ELIAS

units.text: There's a machine at the end. I have quarters.
units.name: ROSALIND

units.text: I'm not hungry.
units.name: ELIAS

units.text: You said that in the car.
units.name: ROSALIND

units.text: Because I wasn't.
units.name: ELIAS

units.text: We have twenty minutes. The judge wants the statement before the lunch recess.
units.name: NOEL

units.text: Does it have to be him who reads it?
units.name: ROSALIND

units.text: It's his statement, Mrs. Harte.
units.name: NOEL

units.text: I wrote half of it.
units.name: ROSALIND

units.text: You wrote all of it.
units.name: ELIAS

units.text: I wrote what you told me.
units.name: ROSALIND

units.text: You wrote what I should have told you.
units.name: ELIAS

units.text: Either way, it needs to be said out loud. The judge wants to hear a voice, not a page.
units.name: NOEL

units.text: And if my voice doesn't work?
units.name: ELIAS

units.text: Then you wait and try again.
units.name: NOEL

units.text: She doesn't give people a second try.
units.name: ELIAS

units.text: She gives them more than you think.
units.name: NOEL

units.text: Noel, do you have children?
units.name: ROSALIND

units.text: Two.
units.name: NOEL

units.text: Then you know it's not about what the judge gives.
units.name: ROSALIND

units.text: I know.
units.name: NOEL

units.text: Elias stands abruptly, walks to the window, and lays his palm flat against the glass.
The radiator knocks again.
Rosalind opens the folder, takes out three typed pages, and smooths them against her knee.
I'll read the first paragraph with you.
units.name: ROSALIND

units.text: Mom.
units.name: ELIAS

units.text: Not for the judge. For the hallway.
units.name: ROSALIND

units.text: Nobody's in the hallway.
units.name: ELIAS

units.text: Then it won't matter if I stumble.
units.name: ROSALIND

units.text: She begins, almost inaudibly, to read.
Elias turns from the window.
Noel steps back toward the fountain, giving them the bench.
